editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. They do break the page's own terminology. Entry 85 leaves "instance" and "endpoint" in English, but everywhere else the page uses "contoh" and "titik akhir". It also calls the link to the verify section "Sahkan keputusan", while the heading itself is "Sahkan hasilnya", and "keputusan" can be read as "decision". Entries 97 and 102 turn the headings into "Fungsi Katalog" and "Fungsi Tersuai", but the text under them (entries 87, 98, 101, 103) keeps the product names "Catalog Functions" and "Custom Functions" in English, so each heading no longer matches its own section.

examples.source: shows what a specific instance has already been granted. Use the **account** endpoint to discover valid values
examples.translation: menunjukkan apa yang telah diberikan kepada instance tertentu. Guna endpoint **account** untuk mengetahui nilai yang sah
examples.suggested: menunjukkan apa yang telah diberikan kepada contoh tertentu. Gunakan titik akhir **account** untuk mengetahui nilai yang sah
examples.why: Everywhere else the page uses 'contoh' for instance and 'titik akhir' for endpoint. This note is the only place that switches to the English words.

examples.source: (see [Verify the result](#verify-result)) ... and the **functions** endpoint to confirm the result.
examples.translation: (lihat [Sahkan keputusan](#verify-result)) ... untuk mengesahkan keputusan.
examples.suggested: (lihat [Sahkan hasilnya](#verify-result)) ... untuk mengesahkan hasilnya.
examples.why: The heading this links to is 'Sahkan hasilnya' (entry 108). 'Keputusan' can also mean 'decision', so it is the less precise word for an API result.

examples.source: Catalog Functions {#catalog-functions}
examples.translation: Fungsi Katalog {#catalog-functions}
examples.suggested: Catalog Functions {#catalog-functions}
examples.why: The text right under this heading (entries 98 and 101) and entry 87 keep 'Catalog Functions' as an English product name. Translating only the heading splits the name in two. The same applies to entry 102, 'Fungsi Tersuai', against 'Custom Functions' in entry 103.

editor_note: All six entries are faithful and read naturally with the standard "anda" register, including "skill" as "kemahiran AI", "AI assistant" as "pembantu AI" and "reusable set of instructions" as "satu set arahan boleh guna semula".

The meaning is faithful all the way through. The key points survive: context-based restrictions "tidak memberikan akses", and the role requirements in [5] (Pentadbir for rules, Editor/Pentadbir for zones, Viewer can only add zones) are intact. There are two wording problems. In [4], "credentials" is rendered as bare "kelayakan", which in Malay reads as "qualifications"; the usual security term is "bukti kelayakan". In [5], the IBM Cloud role label "Viewer" is rendered as "Penonton" (spectator), which is odd for an access role and doesn't match the console label users will see; "Editor" is left in English, so the role labels are handled inconsistently.

examples.source: in the face of compromised or mismanaged credentials
examples.translation: dalam situasi kelayakan yang terjejas atau tidak diurus dengan baik
examples.suggested: walaupun bukti kelayakan telah terjejas atau tidak diurus dengan baik
examples.why: Bare 'kelayakan' usually means qualifications or eligibility. The standard security term for credentials is 'bukti kelayakan'.

examples.source: A user with the Viewer role on the Context-based restrictions service
examples.translation: Pengguna dengan peranan Penonton pada perkhidmatan Sekatan berasaskan konteks
examples.suggested: Pengguna dengan peranan Viewer (Pemapar) pada perkhidmatan Sekatan berasaskan konteks
examples.why: 'Penonton' means spectator and doesn't sound like an access role. It also won't match the IBM Cloud role label the user sees, and 'Editor' is kept in English, so the role names are inconsistent.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. Two places translate the software-versioning idiom "break" word for word. In [3], "memecahkan keserasian" is a calque of "break compatibility"; "tidak serasi dengan semua versi Qiskit sebelumnya" or "memutuskan keserasian" reads more naturally. In [6], "Perubahan pakej yang memecah" is a truncated calque of "breaking changes" that a Malay reader will find unclear.

examples.source: but it does break compatibility with all previous versions of Qiskit
examples.translation: tetapi ia memecahkan keserasian dengan semua versi Qiskit sebelumnya
examples.suggested: tetapi ia tidak lagi serasi dengan semua versi Qiskit sebelumnya
examples.why: 'memecahkan keserasian' translates the English idiom word for word. A native technical writer would say 'tidak serasi' or 'memutuskan keserasian'.

examples.source: Breaking package changes of Qiskit v1.0
examples.translation: Perubahan pakej yang memecah dalam Qiskit v1.0
examples.suggested: Perubahan pakej Qiskit v1.0 yang tidak serasi ke belakang
examples.why: 'yang memecah' ('that breaks') has no object and does not work as a rendering of 'breaking changes'. Saying the changes are not backward-compatible states the meaning clearly.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning, and nothing in them would mislead a learner. Entry 6 has two wording problems. It renders "job" as "pekerjaan" (which suggests employment), while entry 30 and the rest of the page use "kerja". It also coins "terbevektor" for "vectorized", which is not standard Malay, where entry 12 already has "yang divektorkan". Entry 30 is accurate, but it writes "shots" where entry 16 has "shot", a small inconsistency.

examples.source: which executes the defined workload as a job. Then, after the job has completed
examples.translation: yang melaksanakan beban kerja yang ditakrifkan sebagai pekerjaan. Kemudian, selepas pekerjaan selesai
examples.suggested: yang melaksanakan beban kerja yang ditakrifkan sebagai satu kerja. Kemudian, selepas kerja selesai
examples.why: "pekerjaan" means occupation or employment. The rest of the page, including entries 14, 15, 18, 25 and 30, uses "kerja" for a runtime job, so this entry should match.

examples.source: efficiently define vectorized workloads
examples.translation: mentakrifkan beban kerja terbevektor dengan cekap
examples.suggested: mentakrifkan beban kerja yang divektorkan dengan cekap
examples.why: "terbevektor" is not a well-formed Malay word. Entry 12 already uses "yang divektorkan" for "vectorized".

examples.source: particular shots ... Shots are grouped
examples.translation: shots tertentu ... Shots dikumpulkan
examples.suggested: shot tertentu ... Shot dikumpulkan
examples.why: Entry 16 uses the singular "shot" as a count noun ("data shot", "shot yang tersusun"). This entry uses the English plural "shots", so the page is inconsistent.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The Dependabot advice in [3] keeps its meaning, and the addon names come through intact (perambatan balik pengoperasi, pepenjuru kuantum berasaskan sampel, kon cahaya berlorek). Two small fixes are worth making. In [7] and [10], "mapper" (a tool) is rendered "pemetaan" ("mapping", the process); "pemeta" would be the accurate noun. In [3], "Adalah sangat penting..." and "adalah sangat disyorkan agar anda..." copy the English "It is..." sentence pattern; a native technical writer would say "Anda sangat disyorkan menggunakan...".

examples.source: Fermionic mapper Qiskit addon
examples.translation: Tambahan Qiskit pemetaan fermionik
examples.suggested: Tambahan Qiskit pemeta fermionik
examples.why: 'mapper' is the tool, i.e. the thing that maps. 'pemetaan' means the mapping or the process. The same applies to [10], 'pemetaan pengoptimuman'.

examples.source: Therefore, it is strongly recommended that you use security tools like Dependabot
examples.translation: Oleh itu, adalah sangat disyorkan agar anda menggunakan alat keselamatan seperti Dependabot
examples.suggested: Oleh itu, anda sangat disyorkan menggunakan alat keselamatan seperti Dependabot
examples.why: 'adalah sangat disyorkan agar' copies the English 'it is recommended that' pattern. Making 'anda' the subject reads more naturally, and the same applies to 'Adalah sangat penting untuk anda...' at the start of the entry.

editor_note: Both rewritten code-comment entries are faithful and natural: "Dapatkan argumen program" [12] and "Agihkan tugas merentasi pekerja" [14]. "Merentasi" is an established Malay tech rendering of "across", and "pekerja" is a defensible term for compute workers.

The page is about IBM Quantum Platform service instances, but every "instance" is translated as "contoh", which in Malay means "example" or "sample". So the title reads as "the cost incurred by an example", and "Instances page" becomes "halaman Contoh", meaning "Examples page". A reader can't work out what the page is about or find the UI page it points to. Use "instans" (or "tika") throughout: entries 0, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8. There are also smaller slips. The product name "Open plans" is translated as "pelan Terbuka" while "Premium", "Flex" and "Pay-As-You-Go" stay in English. "Rolling" becomes "(bergerak)" and "sehingga masa semasa pada hari semasa" is stiff. A stray period sits inside the link text "[Urus kos.]".

examples.source: View how much cost has been incurred by an instance
examples.translation: Lihat berapa banyak kos yang telah ditanggung oleh sesebuah contoh
examples.suggested: Lihat berapa banyak kos yang telah ditanggung oleh sesebuah instans
examples.why: 'contoh' means 'example', not a cloud service instance. The page's subject is unidentifiable.

examples.source: from the [Instances page](...), click the instance to open its details page
examples.translation: daripada [halaman Contoh](...), klik contoh untuk membuka halaman butirannya
examples.suggested: daripada [halaman Instans](...), klik instans tersebut untuk membuka halaman butirannya
examples.why: 'halaman Contoh' reads as 'Examples page', which sends the user to a page that doesn't exist.

examples.source: For Premium and Open plans, this is the real-time usage for the last 28 days (rolling), up to the current time on the current day.
examples.translation: Untuk pelan Premium dan Terbuka, ini adalah penggunaan masa nyata untuk 28 hari lepas (bergerak), sehingga masa semasa pada hari semasa.
examples.suggested: Untuk pelan Premium dan Open, ini ialah penggunaan masa nyata bagi tempoh 28 hari terakhir (bergulir), sehingga saat ini pada hari ini.
examples.why: The plan name 'Open' is translated but the other plan names are not. '(bergerak)' is an awkward rendering of 'rolling', and 'masa semasa pada hari semasa' is a calque.

examples.source: see [Manage costs](/guides/manage-cost).
examples.translation: lihat [Urus kos.](/guides/manage-cost)
examples.suggested: lihat [Urus kos](/guides/manage-cost).
examples.why: The period has moved inside the link text.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The threshold-theorem caveats (the threshold is finite, it depends on the code and the gate choices, and it does *not* depend on circuit size) and the "never go without protection" point all come through intact. In [4], "decoding" is rendered as "menyahhad", which means "de-limit"; it should be "menyahkod". The nearby "mengekodnya semula" lets a reader recover the meaning, so it does not mislead. The rest is phrasing: "arbitrarily large" is calqued as "besar secara sewenang-wenangnya" (in [5] and [7]), "reliably" is rendered with the Indonesian-flavoured "dengan andal", and "This all presents" is calqued as "Semua ini membentangkan".

examples.source: we certainly can't risk decoding qubits
examples.translation: kita pasti tidak boleh mengambil risiko untuk menyahhad qubit
examples.suggested: kita pasti tidak boleh mengambil risiko menyahkod qubit
examples.why: 'menyahhad' means remove a limit, not decode. It is probably a typo for 'menyahkod', and 'mengekodnya semula' just after it shows the intended meaning.

examples.source: perform arbitrarily large quantum computations reliably using noisy hardware
examples.translation: melakukan pengiraan kuantum yang besar secara sewenang-wenangnya dengan andal
examples.suggested: melaksanakan pengiraan kuantum sebesar mana pun secara boleh dipercayai
examples.why: 'secara sewenang-wenangnya' is a literal calque of 'arbitrarily' that sounds like 'recklessly', and 'andal' reads as Indonesian. The same calque appears again in [7].

examples.source: This all presents a major challenge.
examples.translation: Semua ini membentangkan cabaran besar.
examples.suggested: Semua ini merupakan cabaran besar.
examples.why: 'membentangkan' (to present, as in giving a presentation) is a calque of 'presents'. It is unidiomatic here.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The claim that every state has a purification, with its caveat that the traced-out part must be large enough, is kept in [3], and the dilation intuition in [4] is intact. The problems are three term choices. 'Traced out' is rendered 'dijejaki keluar' ('tracked out'), which is a literal calque that does not tie back to the Malay linear-algebra term for trace, 'surih'. 'Fidelity' is rendered 'kesetiaan' (everyday 'loyalty') where 'fideliti' is the usual technical term, and 'dilation' is rendered 'pelebaran' where the math term is 'dilatasi'. All three are used consistently and a reader can still follow them, so none of them misleads.

examples.source: when the rest of the compound system is traced out
examples.translation: apabila baki sistem kompaun tersebut dijejaki keluar
examples.suggested: apabila baki sistem kompaun tersebut disurih keluar (surih separa)
examples.why: 'Dijejaki' means 'tracked'. The partial-trace operation is 'surih' in Malay linear algebra, and the calque hides that link.

examples.source: the *fidelity* between two quantum states
examples.translation: *kesetiaan* antara dua keadaan kuantum
examples.suggested: *fideliti* antara dua keadaan kuantum
examples.why: 'Kesetiaan' is everyday 'loyalty'. The quantum-information measure is conventionally 'fideliti'.

examples.source: an example of a *dilation* in mathematics
examples.translation: contoh *pelebaran* dalam matematik
examples.suggested: contoh *dilatasi* dalam matematik
examples.why: 'Dilatasi' is the standard Malay mathematical term. 'Pelebaran' reads as plain 'widening'.

editor_note: The meaning holds up across the page, including the tricky parts: the ECR commutation argument [265], the p→1 dephasing subtlety [227] and the CNOT propagation table [280]. The problems are that core terms switch partway through the page. Energy relaxation starts as "kelonggaran tenaga" and becomes "relaksasi tenaga" from [187]. Dephasing appears as "pengurangan fasa", "nyah-fasa" and "defasa". Entanglement appears as "keterjeratan", "keterikatan", "terjalin" and "pengait", gate switches from "gate" to "get" from [237], and "ground state" is written "keadaan dasar" in [94] but "keadaan asas" in [187], which is the same term the page uses for "basis state". Two smaller wording slips: [284] "Selain had keras" says "besides a hard cutoff" where the English means "instead of", and [61] "sehingga beribu-ribu" turns "on the order of thousands" into "up to thousands".

examples.source: Recall that the state $|0\rangle$ is a qubit's ground state
examples.translation: keadaan $|0\rangle$ ialah keadaan asas (ground state) qubit
examples.suggested: keadaan $|0\rangle$ ialah keadaan dasar qubit
examples.why: On this page 'keadaan asas' means 'basis state' (e.g. [25], [136]), and [94] already uses 'keadaan dasar' for ground state. Reusing it here merges the two ideas; the English gloss in brackets is the only thing keeping them apart.

examples.source: Dephasing (loss of phase information)
examples.translation: Pengurangan fasa (kehilangan maklumat fasa)
examples.suggested: Nyahfasa (kehilangan maklumat fasa)
examples.why: 'Pengurangan fasa' means 'phase reduction', not dephasing. The page also uses 'nyah-fasa' [174] and 'defasa' [211], so the same channel has three names.

examples.source: Instead of a hard cutoff, each potential error in the circuit is assigned a graded “shade”
examples.translation: Selain had keras, setiap ralat berpotensi dalam litar diberikan "lorekan" bergred
examples.suggested: Sebagai ganti had keras, setiap ralat berpotensi dalam litar diberikan "lorekan" bergred
examples.why: 'Selain' reads as 'besides/in addition to', so a reader could think shading is added on top of the hard cutoff. The English says shading replaces it.

examples.source: we might plausibly implement on the order of thousands of two-qubit gates
examples.translation: kita mungkin secara munasabah boleh melaksanakan sehingga beribu-ribu gate dua-qubit
examples.suggested: kita mungkin secara munasabah boleh melaksanakan pada tahap beribu-ribu gate dua-qubit
examples.why: 'Sehingga' makes it an upper limit ('up to'), but the English gives an order-of-magnitude estimate.

examples.source: Let's start with energy relaxation errors.
examples.translation: Mari kita mulakan dengan ralat kelonggaran tenaga.
examples.suggested: Use one term throughout (e.g. 'relaksasi tenaga' everywhere)
examples.why: [46]-[91] say 'kelonggaran tenaga' and [187]-[212] say 'relaksasi tenaga' for the same T1 process. A learner may think these are two different things.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the measurement, Pauli-observable, superposition and entanglement sections, and core terms are used consistently (keadaan terbelit/keterbelitan, superposisi, boleh ukur, pemalar penormalan, matriks uniter). A few small things are still worth fixing. [9] adds "penuh misteri" ("full of mystery"), which the English "deceptively simple" does not say. [25] renders "least significant" as "paling tidak bererti", a calque that can read as "most meaningless". [72] turns "a normal measurement does the job" into "ukuran biasa boleh dilakukan" ("can be done"). The page also uses casual "kamu" throughout where the convention is "anda".

examples.source: the deceptively simple Bell state
examples.translation: Bell state yang kelihatan mudah tetapi penuh misteri
examples.suggested: Bell state yang kelihatan mudah
examples.why: Adds 'full of mystery', which is not in the source. The English only means it looks simpler than it is.

examples.source: the first (or least significant) qubit
examples.translation: qubit pertama (atau paling tidak bererti)
examples.suggested: qubit pertama (atau paling kurang signifikan)
examples.why: 'paling tidak bererti' can read as 'most meaningless'. The usual rendering of LSB/MSB is 'paling kurang signifikan' / 'paling signifikan'.

examples.source: After that, a normal measurement does the job.
examples.translation: Selepas itu, ukuran biasa boleh dilakukan.
examples.suggested: Selepas itu, ukuran biasa sudah memadai.
examples.why: The translation says a normal measurement 'can be done', which loses the point that it is enough to get the X-basis result.

examples.source: steps you through the content
examples.translation: membimbing kamu melalui kandungan
examples.suggested: membimbing anda melalui kandungan
examples.why: Uses casual 'kamu' throughout the page instead of the standard 'anda'.

editor_note: All four short prose entries read accurately and naturally ("Simulasi klasik", "Pelajaran ini boleh dianggap pilihan, tetapi amat disyorkan" keeps both the optional status and the strong recommendation); "ditempatkan di GitHub" is acceptable, though "dihoskan di" would be slightly more idiomatic.

Entry 48 is faithful and consistent with the rest of the page. It uses "pilihan pengurangan ralat" for "error mitigation options", keeps the link title "Konfigurasi pengurangan ralat" the same as in entry 42, and leaves the API class names EstimatorOptions and SamplerOptions in English.

Nothing in this translation would mislead a learner, but three small things need fixing. First, the page description in [0] uses the English spelling "quantum" ("hibrid klasik quantum"), while the rest of the file uses "kuantum" ("pengkomputeran kuantum"). Second, "Peperiksaan ini bertujuan untuk diambil" in [6] is a stiff copy of the English passive. Third, in [11] the full stop was moved inside both link texts ("[di sini.]"). "Algoritma variasi" for "variational algorithm" can be defended, but "algoritma variasional" would be the more exact term.

examples.source: hybrid classical quantum algorithms
examples.translation: algoritma hibrid klasik quantum
examples.suggested: algoritma hibrid klasik-kuantum
examples.why: Uses the English spelling 'quantum', but everywhere else the file uses the Malay spelling 'kuantum'.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: Peperiksaan ini bertujuan untuk diambil selepas membaca pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.suggested: Peperiksaan ini sepatutnya diambil selepas anda membaca pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.why: 'bertujuan untuk diambil' copies the English passive word for word and sounds stiff in Malay.

examples.source: can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.translation: boleh dilihat [di sini.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/)
examples.suggested: boleh dilihat [di sini](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.why: The full stop was moved inside the link text, so it becomes part of the link. This happens in both links.

editor_note: Entry 41 renders the heading 'Subspace Search VQE (SSVQE)' as 'Carian Subruang VQE (SSVQE)'. That keeps the English modifier-before-head word order. In Malay the head noun comes first, so the phrase reads as 'the subspace search of VQE' rather than 'a VQE that uses subspace search'. Entry 42 immediately says SSVQE is a VQE variant, so a learner would not be misled. The heading also doesn't match the page's other method names: entry 6 keeps 'Subspace Search VQE' in English, and so do the VQE and VQD headings (entries 11 and 71). Use 'VQE Carian Subruang (SSVQE)', or keep the English name to match entry 6.

examples.source: Subspace Search VQE (SSVQE) {#subspace-search-vqe-ssvqe}
examples.translation: Carian Subruang VQE (SSVQE) {#subspace-search-vqe-ssvqe}
examples.suggested: VQE Carian Subruang (SSVQE) {#subspace-search-vqe-ssvqe}
examples.why: This copies the English word order. Malay puts the head noun first, so 'Carian Subruang VQE' reads as 'subspace search of VQE' rather than a VQE variant. It also doesn't match entry 6, which keeps the English name 'Subspace Search VQE'.

editor_note: Nothing on this index page would mislead a learner. It is only course and module titles, and most read naturally (e.g. "Asas Pembetulan Ralat Kuantum", "Pengkomputeran Kuantum Skala Utiliti"). Three small fixes are still worth making. In [4], "Reka Bentuk dan Pimpin" mixes a noun with an imperative verb, and verbal nouns such as "Mereka Bentuk dan Memimpin" would read better. In [12], "Pepenjuru" means "diagonal", not "diagonalization", which is "Pempenjuruan". In [6], "Fundamental" is a loanword that sits oddly next to the "Asas" used for Basics and Foundations in the other titles.

examples.source: Designing And Leading Quantum Projects
examples.translation: Reka Bentuk dan Pimpin Projek Kuantum
examples.suggested: Mereka Bentuk dan Memimpin Projek Kuantum
examples.why: The English uses gerunds. The Malay pairs a noun (reka bentuk) with a bare imperative verb (pimpin), so the title reads like a command. Verbal nouns keep both halves parallel.

examples.source: Quantum Diagonalization Algorithms
examples.translation: Algoritma Pepenjuru Kuantum
examples.suggested: Algoritma Pempenjuruan Kuantum
examples.why: 'Pepenjuru' means 'diagonal' (the noun or adjective). The standard term for the process of diagonalization is 'pempenjuruan'.

examples.source: Fundamentals Of Quantum Algorithms
examples.translation: Fundamental Algoritma Kuantum
examples.suggested: Prinsip Asas Algoritma Kuantum
examples.why: 'Fundamental' is an English adjective used here as a noun, which is awkward in Malay. 'Prinsip Asas' or 'Dasar' reads naturally while keeping it distinct from 'Asas' for Basics/Foundations.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. Three phrasings are stiff and a native editor would change them. In [5], "tersalah habiskan" (accidentally exhaust) reads as "mistakenly spent"; "secara tidak sengaja menghabiskan" is more natural. In [10], "kebiasaan dengan Python" leans toward "habit" rather than "familiarity"; "sedikit pengetahuan tentang Python" or "biasa dengan Python" reads better. In [4], "mekanik kuantum pengantar" is a calque of "introductory quantum mechanics"; "pengenalan mekanik kuantum" is the usual Malay course-name form.

examples.source: in case students accidentally exhaust their free quantum computing time
examples.translation: sekiranya pelajar tersalah habiskan masa pengkomputeran kuantum percuma mereka
examples.suggested: sekiranya pelajar secara tidak sengaja menghabiskan masa pengkomputeran kuantum percuma mereka
examples.why: 'tersalah' means 'did by mistake/wrongly', which is awkward here; 'secara tidak sengaja' is the natural rendering of 'accidentally'.

examples.source: Some Python familiarity
examples.translation: Sedikit kebiasaan dengan Python
examples.suggested: Sedikit pengetahuan tentang Python
examples.why: 'kebiasaan' primarily means 'habit/custom'; it is a stiff rendering of 'familiarity'.

examples.source: introductory quantum mechanics
examples.translation: mekanik kuantum pengantar
examples.suggested: pengenalan mekanik kuantum
examples.why: This is a word-order calque; Malay course titles normally use 'pengenalan ...' or '... peringkat pengenalan'.

editor_note: Entry 76 is faithful and natural: "superposisi keadaan komputasi ... puncak pada setiap nombor binari ganjil" keeps the odd/even condition that entry 77's answer depends on, and uses the same "komputasi" and "puncak" terms as entries 53 and 70.

Entry 4 is the rewritten H1 and translates "Variational" as "Berubah-ubah". In everyday Malay that word means "fluctuating" or "changing back and forth", so it drops the tie to the variational principle. Everywhere else the file uses "variatif" ("prinsip variatif" in [13], [22] and [81], "algoritma kuantum variatif" in [12]) or keeps the English name ([1], [69]). Placing it after "Kuantum" is also awkward, because it can read as "a fluctuating quantum". The acronym (VQE) and the headings around it keep the concept recognisable, so this is not misleading. It is still an inconsistent, weak term that a native editor would change to "Penyelesai Eigen Kuantum Variatif (VQE)".

examples.source: Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) {#variational-quantum-eigensolver-vqe}
examples.translation: Penyelesai Nilai Eigen Kuantum Berubah-ubah (VQE) {#variational-quantum-eigensolver-vqe}
examples.suggested: Penyelesai Eigen Kuantum Variatif (VQE) {#variational-quantum-eigensolver-vqe}
examples.why: 'Berubah-ubah' means fluctuating or changing, not variational. The file uses 'variatif' everywhere else (e.g. 'prinsip variatif', 'algoritma kuantum variatif' in [12]), so this heading breaks the term's consistency. Its word order also reads like 'fluctuating quantum'.

editor_note: The three entries on this index page are faithful and read naturally: Modules→Modul, Computer Science→Sains Komputer, Quantum Mechanics→Mekanik Kuantum, with the links and anchors left unchanged.

Both rewritten entries are faithful. Entry 26 keeps the undetermined-until-measured claim, the collapse to +z/-z, the electron being "bertentangan tepat dengan positron", "tindakan seram dari jauh" and "fizik bukan setempat". Entry 29 keeps "berdekad" and uses the file's usual capitalised "Anda".

All four rewritten entries (57, 81, 89, 116) are faithful and would not mislead a learner. Two small surface slips remain. In entry 57, "by hand" is calqued as "secara tangan", where a Malay technical writer would say "secara manual" or "dengan tangan". Entry 116 is an imperative instruction ("Terangkan ...") but ends in a stray question mark, and "mendorong ini ke had mutlak" reads stiffly. Entries 81 and 89 are fine as written.

examples.source: Calculate the uncertainty of $X$ in the state $|+\rangle_y = |+i\rangle$, by hand.
examples.translation: Kira ketidakpastian $X$ dalam keadaan $|+\rangle_y = |+i\rangle$, secara tangan.
examples.suggested: Kira ketidakpastian $X$ dalam keadaan $|+\rangle_y = |+i\rangle$ secara manual.
examples.why: "secara tangan" is a literal calque of "by hand". The idiomatic Malay is "secara manual" or "dengan tangan".

examples.source: Explain how you would push this to the absolute limit, making $\langle Y \rangle$ as large as possible.
examples.translation: Terangkan bagaimana anda akan mendorong ini ke had mutlak, menjadikan $\langle Y \rangle$ sebesar mungkin?
examples.suggested: Terangkan bagaimana anda akan membawa ini ke had mutlaknya, dengan menjadikan $\langle Y \rangle$ sebesar mungkin.
examples.why: The imperative sentence wrongly ends with a question mark. "mendorong ini ke had mutlak" is a stiff calque of "push this to the absolute limit".

editor_note: All five rewritten entries (123-125, 127, 129) keep the English meaning. The control/target condition, the ket order |BA⟩ with the control on the right, the XOR definition and the matrix basis order all match the source. The problems are terminology and phrasing. Entries 124 and 125 translate "basis state" and "computational basis" as "keadaan basis" and "nilai basis pengiraan", but the rest of the page uses "keadaan asas (pengiraan)" (entries 67, 89, 93, 96). Entries 123-125 also write "gate" where nearby CNOT prose uses "get" (entries 132, 134). Two phrasings read as translated from English: "biar A=q_0 menjadi kawalan" copies English "let", and "terbalik" for "flips" means "upside down" rather than a bit flip.

examples.source: Qiskit writes two-qubit basis states as $\vert q_1q_0\rangle$.
examples.translation: Qiskit menulis keadaan basis dua-qubit sebagai $\vert q_1q_0\rangle$.
examples.suggested: Qiskit menulis keadaan asas dua-qubit sebagai $\vert q_1q_0\rangle$.
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'keadaan asas' / 'keadaan asas pengiraan' for basis states (entries 67, 93). Switching to 'basis' only here splits the term.

examples.source: For computational basis values $a,b\in\{0,1\}$ of qubits $A$ and $B$, the gate acts as follows:
examples.translation: Untuk nilai basis pengiraan $a,b\in\{0,1\}$ bagi qubit $A$ dan $B$, gate bertindak seperti berikut:
examples.suggested: Untuk nilai asas pengiraan $a,b\in\{0,1\}$ bagi qubit $A$ dan $B$, get ini bertindak seperti berikut:
examples.why: 'basis pengiraan' clashes with 'asas pengiraan' used elsewhere on the page. 'gate' here clashes with the 'get' used in nearby CNOT prose (132, 134).

examples.source: Here, let $A=q_0$ be the control and $B=q_1$ be the target
examples.translation: Di sini, biar $A=q_0$ menjadi kawalan dan $B=q_1$ menjadi sasaran
examples.suggested: Di sini, katakan $A=q_0$ ialah kawalan dan $B=q_1$ ialah sasaran
examples.why: 'biar ... menjadi' copies English 'let ... be'. Malay mathematical writing uses 'katakan' or 'andaikan'.

examples.source: while the target value $b$ flips when $a=1$.
examples.translation: manakala nilai sasaran $b$ terbalik apabila $a=1$.
examples.suggested: manakala nilai sasaran $b$ bertukar (dibalikkan) apabila $a=1$.
examples.why: 'terbalik' suggests 'upside down / overturned'. The page itself uses 'dibalikkan' for a bit flip (entry 150).

editor_note: The rewritten entry 49 keeps the meaning of the English. Aligned particles still go to the maximum deflection toward the stronger side ("sisi yang lebih kuat") and anti-aligned particles toward the weaker side ("sisi yang lebih lemah"), with a smooth range of deflections in between, so it does not mislead. The one problem is "bertentangan sejajar" for "anti-aligned". The word order is back to front and reads awkwardly. Entry 38 on the same page words the idea more naturally as "sejajar ... bertentangan", so "sejajar bertentangan" (or "antisejajar") would read better and match it.

examples.source: those particles that started out anti-aligned with the external field
examples.translation: zarah-zarah yang bermula dalam keadaan bertentangan sejajar dengan medan luaran
examples.suggested: zarah-zarah yang bermula dalam keadaan sejajar bertentangan dengan medan luaran
examples.why: "bertentangan sejajar" puts the words in the wrong order for Malay and reads stiffly. "sejajar bertentangan" or "antisejajar" is the natural phrase and matches how entry 38 words it ("sejajar sempurna bertentangan"). The meaning is correct either way.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The key technical claims survive intact: the target circuit has less Trotter error than the comparison circuit ([39], [42]), the split at t=4/t=5 is kept ([24], [26]), and "fidelity" is consistently "kesetiaan". A native editor would still fix a few stiff spots. "Map to quantum problem" is rendered with the noun "Peta" where the imperative verb "Petakan" is needed ([4], [17]). "Initialize our problem's Hamiltonian" becomes "Mulakan Hamiltonian", which reads as "start/begin the Hamiltonian" ([5]). "for simplicity" is rendered as the dangling "untuk memudahkan" ([14]).

examples.source: **Step 1: Map to quantum problem**
examples.translation: **Langkah 1: Peta ke masalah kuantum**
examples.suggested: **Langkah 1: Petakan kepada masalah kuantum**
examples.why: 'Peta' is the noun 'map'. A step heading needs the imperative verb 'Petakan'. The same issue appears in [17].

examples.source: Initialize our problem's Hamiltonian and observable(s)
examples.translation: Mulakan Hamiltonian masalah kita dan observable(s)
examples.suggested: Tetapkan Hamiltonian dan observable masalah kita
examples.why: 'Mulakan' means 'start/begin', which does not fit setting up a Hamiltonian. The English '(s)' plural marker is also left in the Malay.

examples.source: Use a fake backend for simplicity
examples.translation: Gunakan backend palsu untuk memudahkan
examples.suggested: Gunakan backend palsu demi kesederhanaan
examples.why: 'untuk memudahkan' needs an object ('to make ___ easier'), so the phrase is left dangling. 'demi kesederhanaan' or 'supaya mudah' reads naturally.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The key technical passage in [20] (Move = reset on the second qubit, then SWAP; the destination qubit must share no entanglement, or the rest of the system partially collapses), the qubit reuse in [21] and the caveat that cut_wires cannot reuse qubit wires in [22] are all kept correctly. The remaining issues are editorial. 'Quasiprobability' is rendered as 'kuasikemungkinan', but the conventional word for probability is 'kebarangkalian' ('kemungkinan' means possibility or likelihood). 'keterjalinann' is misspelled. A few phrases are calques: 'Untuk ini berfungsi', 'di tempatnya', 'melakukan Transpile pada'.

examples.source: joint quasiprobability distribution
examples.translation: taburan kuasikemungkinan bersama
examples.suggested: taburan kuasi-kebarangkalian bersama
examples.why: The standard Malay term for probability is 'kebarangkalian'; 'kemungkinan' means possibility or likelihood, so the term is recognizable but imprecise.

examples.source: For this to work as intended, it is important that the second (destination) qubit share no entanglement
examples.translation: Untuk ini berfungsi seperti yang diharapkan, adalah penting bahawa qubit kedua (destinasi) tidak berkongsi sebarang keterjalinann
examples.suggested: Supaya arahan ini berfungsi seperti yang diharapkan, qubit kedua (destinasi) mestilah tidak berkongsi sebarang keterjalinan
examples.why: The sentence copies English syntax ('Untuk ini berfungsi', 'adalah penting bahawa') and misspells 'keterjalinan'.

examples.source: with one additional qubit and the `Move` operations in place
examples.translation: dengan satu qubit tambahan dan operasi `Move` di tempatnya
examples.suggested: dengan satu qubit tambahan serta operasi `Move` yang telah diletakkan
examples.why: 'di tempatnya' is a literal calque of 'in place' and reads awkwardly.

examples.source: We must transpile the circuits with our backend as the target
examples.translation: Kita mesti melakukan Transpile pada Circuit dengan Backend kita sebagai sasaran
examples.suggested: Kita mesti mentranspil litar dengan backend kita sebagai sasaran
examples.why: 'melakukan Transpile pada' is a stiff periphrastic construction; a native writer would use the verb directly.

examples.source: Step 1: Map
examples.translation: Langkah 1: Peta
examples.suggested: Langkah 1: Petakan
examples.why: 'Peta' is the noun 'map'. The other step headings use verbs (Optimumkan, Laksanakan), so this should be the verb 'Petakan'.

editor_note: In entry [0], "sample-based quantum diagonalization" is translated as "pengurusan petak kuantum berasaskan sampel", which means roughly "sample-based quantum square/plot management". That wrongly describes SQD, an addon that diagonalizes a Hamiltonian, and a learner would come away with a false idea of what it does. It should use the diagonalization term (pempepenjuruan) or keep the English name, as the table in [6] does. A smaller issue: "error mitigation" in [6] is given as "pengurangan ralat" ("error reduction"), which is recognizable, but "mitigasi ralat" is the more precise conventional term. The rest of the page is faithful and natural, e.g. "penyebaran balik pengendali" and "anggaran keadaan dasar".

examples.source: sample-based quantum diagonalization
examples.translation: pengurusan petak kuantum berasaskan sampel
examples.suggested: pempepenjuruan kuantum berasaskan sampel
examples.why: 'pengurusan petak' means 'management of squares/plots', not diagonalization. This gives a false idea of what the SQD addon does.

examples.source: Propagated Noise Absorption for error mitigation
examples.translation: Propagated Noise Absorption untuk pengurangan ralat
examples.suggested: Propagated Noise Absorption untuk mitigasi ralat
examples.why: 'Error mitigation' is a specific technique family that is distinct from error reduction or correction. 'mitigasi ralat' is the more precise conventional rendering.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 64 is faithful in meaning: it keeps EstimatorV2 with the fake backend, both circuits (AQC-optimised and the Trotter baseline) and a ZZ measurement for each. The only problem is terminology: it leaves 'observable' in English ('observable ZZ'), but earlier on the same page (entries 41 and 42) the term is translated as 'boleh cerap'. It should use 'boleh cerap ZZ' so the term matches the rest of the page.

examples.source: measuring the ZZ observable for each.
examples.translation: mengukur observable ZZ bagi setiap satu.
examples.suggested: mengukur boleh cerap ZZ bagi setiap litar.
examples.why: Entries 41 and 42 translate 'observable' as 'boleh cerap', so leaving it in English here makes the page inconsistent. 'bagi setiap litar' also reads more naturally than 'bagi setiap satu'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The teleportation steps, the Pauli-correction conditions (X on qubit 3, Z on qubit 0), the MSE reasoning (lower means higher fidelity) and the CDF explanation all match the source. The problem is terminology. 'Feedforward' appears five ways: 'suap balik klasik ke depan' [6,11], 'suap balik ke depan' [14], 'suap balas' [32], 'suap-balik' [17] and untranslated 'feedforward' [49]; 'suap balas'/'suap balik' on their own normally mean feedback. 'Fidelity' appears as 'kesetiaan' [7], 'ketepatan' (which means accuracy) [15-17] and untranslated 'fidelity' [49]. 'Entanglement' also switches between 'pembelitan', 'keterikatan', 'terikat' and 'melilit', and there is some stiff phrasing in [32] and [49].

examples.source: Mid-circuit measurements and feedforward:
examples.translation: Pengukuran litar tengah dan suap balas:
examples.suggested: Pengukuran litar tengah dan suapan ke hadapan (feedforward):
examples.why: 'Suap balas' means feedback, which is the opposite direction of information flow. Other entries use three more variants, and [49] leaves 'feedforward' in English.

examples.source: as a simple metric of entanglement fidelity
examples.translation: sebagai metrik mudah untuk ketepatan pembelitan
examples.suggested: sebagai metrik mudah untuk kesetiaan (fidelity) pembelitan
examples.why: 'Ketepatan' means accuracy. Entry [7] uses 'kesetiaan' and [49] leaves 'fidelity' untranslated, so the key metric has three names in one file.

examples.source: They "undo" the random Pauli flips that occur due to projecting qubits 1 and 2
examples.translation: Ia "membatalkan" balik Pauli rawak yang berlaku akibat memproyeksikan qubit 1 dan 2
examples.suggested: Ia "membatalkan" balikan Pauli rawak yang berlaku akibat pengunjuran qubit 1 dan 2
examples.why: 'Membatalkan balik Pauli rawak' reads as 'undo back random Pauli'. The noun 'flips' has become an adverb, which blurs what gets corrected.

examples.source: the fraction of qubit pairs that have at most that MSE on the y-axis
examples.translation: pecahan pasangan qubit yang mempunyai MSE paling banyak sebanyak itu pada paksi-y
examples.suggested: pecahan pasangan qubit yang MSE-nya tidak melebihi nilai tersebut pada paksi-y
examples.why: 'Paling banyak sebanyak itu' is a clumsy calque of 'at most'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and the physics survives intact: frustration, i.i.d. couplings ("tak bersandar dan teragih secara sama"), variance scaling and the NP-hard ground state. The problems are small wording slips in the background section. In [11], "glassy behavior" stays half in English as "tingkah laku glassy", and "spin glass" is not given its Malay form "kaca spin". Also in [11], "rugged" is rendered "berombak-ombak" ("wavy"), which loses the jagged, many-minima picture; "kasar"/"bergerigi" fits better. In [37], "gunakan options" leaves a bare English common noun in running prose.

examples.source: which is the hallmark of glassy behavior
examples.translation: iaitu ciri utama tingkah laku glassy
examples.suggested: iaitu ciri utama tingkah laku seperti kaca (glassy)
examples.why: An English adjective is left bare inside Malay syntax, so the line reads as unfinished translation.

examples.source: a highly complex, "rugged", energy landscape
examples.translation: landskap tenaga yang sangat kompleks dan "berombak-ombak"
examples.suggested: landskap tenaga yang sangat kompleks dan "kasar/bergerigi"
examples.why: 'Berombak-ombak' suggests smooth waves; 'rugged' is meant to convey a jagged landscape with many local minima.

examples.source: Optionally, use options for additional control over the submission:
examples.translation: Secara pilihan, gunakan options untuk kawalan tambahan terhadap penghantaran:
examples.suggested: Jika perlu, gunakan `options` (pilihan) untuk kawalan tambahan terhadap penghantaran:
examples.why: 'options' is left as a bare English noun and not marked as a parameter name, and 'Secara pilihan' is a stiff calque.

editor_note: Entry [77] reverses the dependency. The English says the boxing and noise-learning steps rely on the preserved two-qubit layer structure, but the Malay says the structure depends on those steps. That breaks the stated reason for using optimization_level=0. The second half of the file also drifts on terminology: 'noise' switches from 'hingar' to 'bunyi' (ordinary 'sound') in [136], [137], [143], [149] and [153]. 'Propagated/propagate' appears as 'terpropagat', 'terhantar' ([6]) and 'merambatkan' ([149]). 'Observable' appears as 'pemerhati' and as bare 'observable' ([6], [135], [149]). 'Randomization' appears as 'rawakisasi' and 'pengacakan'/'diacak' ([138], [150]). There are also small slips: 'melangkau' (skip) is used where 'melangkaui' (go beyond) is meant in [81], and English 'Sample'/'instantiate' is left untranslated in [139] and [140].

examples.source: That structure is what the boxing and noise-learning steps rely on, so a higher optimization level ... must be avoided here.
examples.translation: Struktur itulah yang bergantung kepada langkah pengotakan dan pembelajaran hingar, jadi tahap pengoptimuman yang lebih tinggi ... mesti dielakkan di sini.
examples.suggested: Struktur itulah yang menjadi sandaran langkah pengotakan dan pembelajaran hingar, jadi tahap pengoptimuman yang lebih tinggi ... mesti dielakkan di sini.
examples.why: The dependency is reversed. The Malay says the structure depends on the boxing and noise-learning steps, when those steps actually rely on the structure. That muddles why the optimization level has to stay at 0.

examples.source: We set each noise layer's scale to `0.0` to prevent any additional noise from being injected
examples.translation: Kita tetapkan skala setiap lapisan bunyi kepada `0.0` untuk mengelakkan sebarang bunyi tambahan
examples.suggested: Kita tetapkan skala setiap lapisan hingar kepada `0.0` untuk mengelakkan sebarang hingar tambahan
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'hingar' for noise. From here on it switches to 'bunyi', which means acoustic sound. Entries 137, 143, 149 and 153 have the same problem.

examples.source: propagating inverse noise channels into the observable
examples.translation: merambatkan saluran bunyi songsang ke dalam observable
examples.suggested: mempropagatkan saluran hingar songsang ke dalam pemerhati
examples.why: This one phrase breaks three conventions set elsewhere in the file: 'mempropagatkan' for propagate, 'hingar' for noise and 'pemerhati' for observable.

examples.source: which goes beyond simply identifying two-qubit layers
examples.translation: yang melangkau lebih daripada sekadar mengenal pasti lapisan dua-qubit
examples.suggested: yang melangkaui lebih daripada sekadar mengenal pasti lapisan dua-qubit
examples.why: 'Melangkau' means 'to skip', not 'to go beyond'. As written, the sentence reads as if the method skips identifying layers.

examples.source: We simply instantiate the `Executor` object
examples.translation: Kita cuma instantiate objek `Executor`
examples.suggested: Kita hanya perlu mencipta instans objek `Executor`
examples.why: The English verb 'instantiate' is left untranslated inside Malay syntax, and 'Sample' in [139] has the same problem. Elsewhere the file uses 'instans' and 'mempersampelkan'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The caveats in [43], [50] and [55] survive: MEM is not an isolated DD comparison, MEM cannot retroactively change mid-circuit results, and the plot has no DD or uncertainty curves. In [11], "streamlined transpilation API" became "API transpilasi teragih", which means "distributed". That is the wrong word, though it is too peripheral to mislead a learner in any way that matters. Other slips a native editor would fix: feedforward is rendered as the unusual "gerak maju hadapan" instead of "suapan hadapan"; "omit" became "mengabaikan" (ignore); "routed" became the awkward "dilaluikan", while [40] uses "penghalaan"; and "earlier run" became "larian awal" (initial run).

examples.source: Use Orbit's streamlined transpilation API
examples.translation: Gunakan API transpilasi teragih Orbit
examples.suggested: Gunakan API transpilasi Orbit yang diperkemas
examples.why: 'teragih' means distributed, which is a property the source never claims; 'streamlined' means simplified.

examples.source: mid-circuit measurements with feedforward
examples.translation: pengukuran pertengahan-litar dengan gerak maju hadapan
examples.suggested: pengukuran pertengahan-litar dengan suapan hadapan (feedforward)
examples.why: 'gerak maju hadapan' is a clumsy coinage. 'suapan hadapan' is the conventional Malay control-theory term. Same issue in [50].

examples.source: Both implementations omit the final swap network.
examples.translation: Kedua-dua pelaksanaan mengabaikan rangkaian tukar-ganti akhir.
examples.suggested: Kedua-dua pelaksanaan tidak menyertakan rangkaian swap akhir.
examples.why: 'mengabaikan' means ignore or neglect, but the source means 'deliberately leave out'.

examples.source: mapped and routed by the transpiler
examples.translation: dipetakan dan dilaluikan oleh transpiler
examples.suggested: dipetakan dan dihalakan oleh transpiler
examples.why: 'dilaluikan' is awkward and does not match 'penghalaan', which [40] uses for routing.

examples.source: a successful earlier run with Orbit
examples.translation: larian awal yang berjaya dengan Orbit
examples.suggested: larian terdahulu yang berjaya dengan Orbit
examples.why: 'awal' reads as 'initial/early', not 'previous'.

editor_note: Entry 10 says the same thing as the English: the Li-S battery research link, energy change as the Li-S bond breaks ("ikatan Li-S putus") and reaction pathways and catalysts ("pemangkin") are all there, with nothing added or softened. The one problem is terminology. Entry 10 renders "potential energy surfaces" as "permukaan tenaga keupayaan", but entries 0 and 9 use "permukaan tenaga potensi" for the same concept, which the page abbreviates as PES. "Tenaga keupayaan" is the standard DBP term, so this is a consistency slip, not an error, but a learner may not see that the two phrases mean the same PES. Change entry 10 to "potensi" to match the rest of the page.

examples.source: More broadly, potential energy surfaces are tools for studying reaction pathways
examples.translation: Secara lebih luas, permukaan tenaga keupayaan adalah alat untuk mengkaji laluan tindak balas
examples.suggested: Secara lebih luas, permukaan tenaga potensi ialah alat untuk mengkaji laluan tindak balas
examples.why: Entries 0 and 9 already use "permukaan tenaga potensi (PES)" for this concept. Mixing "keupayaan" and "potensi" on one page makes readers wonder whether they are different things. "ialah" also reads better than "adalah" before a noun phrase.

editor_note: Entry 4 is accurate and reads naturally. "Anggaran penggunaan: Sembilan saat pada pemproses Heron r2" keeps the quantity and the processor name, and the caveat is intact as "NOTA: Ini hanyalah anggaran. Masa jalan anda mungkin berbeza."

The meaning is faithful all the way through. The numbers, the ε clipping, the ~49% limit and the -0.62/-1.50 energy comparison all match the English, and I found no drift that would mislead a learner. The terminology is weak in places. "Variational" is calqued as "berubah-ubah" ("fluctuating") in [15] and [54]. "Continuous" is rendered "berterusan" ("ongoing") instead of the mathematical term "selanjar". "Keadaan asas" is used for both "ground state" ([20], [71]) and "basis states" ([57]). Two terms also switch rendering inside the file: "relaksasi" becomes "pelonggaran" in [81], and "kombinatorial" becomes "gabungan" in [81]. A few calques remain, such as "berkurangan secara tepat kepada" in [21] and "berlaku menjadi" and "meresap" in [67].

examples.source: Variational parameters are randomly initialized.
examples.translation: Parameter berubah-ubah dimulakan secara rawak.
examples.suggested: Parameter variasi dimulakan secara rawak.
examples.why: 'berubah-ubah' means 'fluctuating', not 'variational'. It is also used for 'variational loop' in [54] ('gelung berubah-ubah').

examples.source: The brute-force search over all $2^n$ basis states
examples.translation: Carian brute-force ke atas semua $2^n$ keadaan asas
examples.suggested: Carian brute-force ke atas semua $2^n$ keadaan basis
examples.why: 'keadaan asas' is used for 'ground state' in [20], [46] and [71]. Using it for 'basis states' here merges two different concepts.

examples.source: try modeling different combinatorial problems, or using different solvers for the continuous relaxation
examples.translation: cuba memodelkan masalah gabungan yang berbeza, atau menggunakan penyelesai yang berbeza untuk pelonggaran berterusan
examples.suggested: cuba memodelkan masalah kombinatorial yang berbeza, atau menggunakan penyelesai yang berbeza untuk relaksasi selanjar
examples.why: This is inconsistent with 'kombinatorial' in [14] and 'relaksasi' everywhere else in the file. Also, 'berterusan' ('ongoing') is not the mathematical term for 'continuous'.

examples.source: At $\varepsilon = 0.5$, WS-QAOA reduces exactly to standard QAOA.
examples.translation: Pada $\varepsilon = 0.5$, WS-QAOA berkurangan secara tepat kepada QAOA standard.
examples.suggested: Pada $\varepsilon = 0.5$, WS-QAOA menjadi sama sepenuhnya dengan QAOA standard.
examples.why: This is a calque: 'berkurangan' means 'decreases in amount', not 'reduces to (a special case)'.

examples.source: the optimal partition happened to be the most frequently sampled outcome even from a diffuse state
examples.translation: sekatan optimum berlaku menjadi hasil yang paling kerap disampel walaupun daripada keadaan yang meresap
examples.suggested: sekatan optimum kebetulan menjadi hasil yang paling kerap disampel walaupun daripada keadaan yang tersebar
examples.why: 'berlaku menjadi' is a stiff calque of 'happened to be', and 'meresap' ('seep') is the wrong word for a diffuse state.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout: the X/H gate behaviour, CNOT control/target logic, Bell/GHZ targets and the Qiskit pattern steps all match the English, and no sentence would mislead a learner. The register is the main problem. From about [54] onward the text switches between standard "anda" and colloquial slang ("korang", "jom", "ni", "tu", "je", "tak"), and it goes back and forth inside a single section ([103] and [106] use "anda", [77] and [60] use "korang"). The terms are also inconsistent: "circuit" appears as "Circuit", "quantum circuit(s)" and "litar kuantum" ([101]). Quantum interference in [47] is rendered as "gangguan" (disturbance) instead of the standard "interferens", and the headings [62] and [76] plus the licence sentence [122] were left in English.

examples.source: Great job! Now that you've understood the single-qubit gates, let us look at gates operating on multiple qubits.
examples.translation: Bagus! Sekarang yang korang dah faham tentang single-qubit gate, jom kita tengok gate yang beroperasi pada berbilang qubit.
examples.suggested: Bagus! Setelah anda memahami get satu-qubit, mari kita lihat get yang beroperasi pada berbilang qubit.
examples.why: Uses the colloquial 'korang/dah/jom/tengok' while other entries in the same page use standard 'anda'. The register is inconsistent and too slangy for documentation.

examples.source: the quantum phase is what enables interference between quantum states
examples.translation: fasa kuantum inilah yang membolehkan gangguan antara keadaan kuantum
examples.suggested: fasa kuantum inilah yang membolehkan interferens antara keadaan kuantum
examples.why: 'Gangguan' reads as disturbance or noise. The standard Malay physics term for wave or quantum interference is 'interferens'.

examples.source: by building quantum circuits to generate the desired quantum state
examples.translation: dengan membina litar kuantum untuk menjana keadaan kuantum yang dikehendaki
examples.suggested: Use one rendering for 'circuit' across the whole file
examples.why: Elsewhere the file uses 'Circuit kuantum' or the English 'quantum circuit(s)'. Here, and only here, it switches to 'litar kuantum'.

examples.source: 4. Quantum Quiz with Multi-Qubit Gates
examples.translation: 4. Quantum Quiz with Multi-Qubit gates
examples.suggested: 4. Kuiz Kuantum dengan Get Berbilang Qubit
examples.why: The section heading was left untranslated. [62] has the same problem ('Practices: Quantum Circuits Using Single-Qubit gates').

examples.source: is one of the so-called Bell states
examples.translation: merupakan salah satu daripada [Bell states] yang dipanggil begitu
examples.suggested: merupakan salah satu daripada apa yang dipanggil keadaan Bell
examples.why: 'yang dipanggil begitu' is a stiff calque of 'so-called' and is placed after the noun.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The CNOT condition, the GHZ expectation-value reasoning, the resilience-level trade-off and the no-FTL caveat on teleportation all match the English. The terminology is inconsistent, though. Entanglement is rendered three ways ("terbelit" [64,105], "berentang" [152-153], "keberangkutan" [156]). Circuit switches from "quantum circuits" to "litar" and then to capitalized "Circuit" from [133] onward. Gate appears as both "gate" and "get" ([75], [115]). Encoding is split between "mengekod/pengekodan" and "enkod/mengenkod". Noise is rendered once as "bunyi" [75], which means acoustic sound, while "hingar" is used everywhere else. "Post-process" is rendered as "memproses semula" (reprocess) in [88] and [104], and "python instance" as "contoh Python" (Python example) in [82]. The whole file uses "kamu" rather than "anda", and the later sections drift into colloquial Malay ("dah tengok macam mana nak enkod").

examples.source: **Create entanglement:** Generate a Bell pair between `a` and `b`.
examples.translation: **Cipta keberangkutan:** Jana pasangan Bell antara `a` dan `b`.
examples.suggested: **Cipta keterbelitan:** Jana pasangan Bell antara `a` dan `b`. (pick one of terbelit/keterbelitan and use it in [64], [105], [152]-[153] as well)
examples.why: This is the third different Malay rendering of entanglement in the file. A learner may not recognize these as one concept.

examples.source: by reducing the effects of error and noise
examples.translation: dengan mengurangkan kesan ralat dan bunyi
examples.suggested: dengan mengurangkan kesan ralat dan hingar
examples.why: "Bunyi" means acoustic sound. Everywhere else the file correctly uses "hingar" for quantum noise.

examples.source: where you might postprocess your results
examples.translation: di mana kamu mungkin memproses semula keputusan
examples.suggested: di mana anda mungkin melakukan pasca-pemprosesan ke atas keputusan
examples.why: "Memproses semula" means reprocess, not post-process. The same problem appears in the heading at [104] ("Proses semula keputusan").

examples.source: wait until either the job is completed within your current python instance
examples.translation: tunggu sehingga kerja selesai dalam contoh Python semasa
examples.suggested: tunggu sehingga kerja selesai dalam sesi/instans Python semasa
examples.why: "Contoh" means example. That is the wrong sense of "instance" here, which refers to a running Python session.

examples.source: Hence we have seen how to encode information using rotational gates.
examples.translation: Jadi kita dah tengok macam mana nak enkod maklumat menggunakan gate putaran.
examples.suggested: Oleh itu, kita telah melihat cara mengekod maklumat menggunakan gate putaran.
examples.why: This is colloquial spoken Malay ("dah tengok macam mana nak"), and it uses "enkod" where earlier sections use "mengekod". Together with "kamu" throughout, the register is inconsistent with the "anda" convention.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Criterion numbering, the GHZ and T1 expectations, and the readout-error setup all match the English, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are wording and consistency. Entries [4]–[32] address the reader as "kamu", then [47] onward switches to "anda". "Noisy simulator" becomes "simulator bermasalah" ("problematic simulator") in [43], although the rest of the file uses "bising"/"hingar". "Fidelity" is "ketepatan" in [15]/[25]/[26] but "kesetiaan" in [80]. There are also a few calques: "dalam urutan ratusan mikrodetik" for "on the order of" in [82], "dalam tindakan" for "in action" in [61] and [72], "bermula segar" in [36], and "mereka" referring to criteria in [12].

examples.source: use a noisy simulator based on `FakeVigo`
examples.translation: gunakan simulator bermasalah berdasarkan `FakeVigo`
examples.suggested: gunakan simulator bising berdasarkan `FakeVigo`
examples.why: 'bermasalah' means faulty/problematic, not noisy. It is also inconsistent with 'simulator bising' in [22].

examples.source: the effect of finite T₁, T₂ on algorithm fidelity
examples.translation: kesan T₁, T₂ terhad pada kesetiaan algoritma
examples.suggested: kesan T₁, T₂ terhad pada ketepatan algoritma
examples.why: Fidelity is 'ketepatan' elsewhere in the file ([15], [25], [26]). 'kesetiaan' reads as 'loyalty'.

examples.source: coherence times on the order of hundreds of microseconds
examples.translation: masa koherensi dalam urutan ratusan mikrodetik
examples.suggested: masa koherensi dalam lingkungan ratusan mikrodetik
examples.why: This calques 'on the order of' as 'dalam urutan' ('in a sequence'). A Malay writer would say 'dalam lingkungan' or 'sekitar'.

examples.source: You should see two tall bars on the histogram
examples.translation: Kamu sepatutnya melihat dua bar tinggi pada histogram
examples.suggested: Anda sepatutnya melihat dua bar tinggi pada histogram
examples.why: The file uses 'kamu' up to [32] and 'anda' from [47] on. Standard 'anda' should be used throughout.

examples.source: the ability to start fresh in |0…0〉 is available
examples.translation: keupayaan untuk bermula segar dalam |0…0〉 tersedia
examples.suggested: keupayaan untuk bermula semula dari keadaan bersih |0…0〉 tersedia
examples.why: 'bermula segar' is a literal calque of 'start fresh' and is not idiomatic Malay.

editor_note: I found no semantic drift. Conditions, quantities and caveats (T1 decay, 2% readout error, CCX flipping only when both controls are 1) all match the English. Terminology is inconsistent in places: entanglement appears as "terbelit" [16,17], "keterjeratan" [46,66,68] and "terjalin/keterjalinnya" [68,69]; fidelity appears as both "ketepatan" [15,23,24] and "kesetiaan" [76]; dephasing is left in English in [18] but rendered "defasaan" in [36]. The register also switches from casual "kamu" (entries 4–30) to "anda" (entries 44–79), and there are a few calques ("bermula segar", "selamat mengkomputer kuantum", "daripada 100%" for "instead of 100%").

examples.source: let's construct a small entangled state (GHZ state)
examples.translation: jom bina keadaan terbelit kecil (keadaan GHZ)
examples.suggested: jom bina keadaan terjerat kecil (keadaan GHZ)
examples.why: Entanglement is rendered as terbelit here, keterjeratan in [46]/[66] and terjalin in [68]/[69]. The file should use one term, e.g. terjerat/keterjeratan.

examples.source: the effect of finite T₁, T₂ on algorithm fidelity
examples.translation: kesan T₁, T₂ terhingga pada kesetiaan algoritma
examples.suggested: kesan T₁, T₂ terhingga pada ketepatan algoritma
examples.why: Fidelity is ketepatan in [15], [23] and [24] but kesetiaan here.

examples.source: instead of 100% in `000`/`111`, some probability leaks
examples.translation: daripada 100% dalam `000`/`111`, sebahagian kebarangkalian bocor
examples.suggested: bukannya 100% dalam `000`/`111`, sebahagian kebarangkalian bocor
examples.why: 'daripada' can be read as 'out of 100%', which blurs 'instead of'. 'bukannya' makes the contrast clear.

examples.source: the ability to start fresh in |0…0〉 is available
examples.translation: keupayaan untuk bermula segar dalam |0…0〉 tersedia
examples.suggested: keupayaan untuk bermula semula dari keadaan bersih |0…0〉 tersedia
examples.why: 'bermula segar' is a literal calque of 'start fresh' and reads unnaturally in Malay.

examples.source: You should observe the probability `P(qubit=1)` decreasing
examples.translation: Anda sepatutnya dapat melihat kebarangkalian `P(qubit=1)` berkurang
examples.suggested: Anda sepatutnya dapat melihat kebarangkalian `P(qubit=1)` berkurang (and change the earlier 'kamu' to 'anda' to match)
examples.why: Entries 4–30 address the reader as 'kamu' and entries 44–79 as 'anda'. The standard convention is 'anda' throughout.
